title: Yulu Enters Nashik With 100 Electric Two-Wheelers for Delivery Riders
excerpt: Nashik becomes Yulu's 13th city and its second in Maharashtra, as daily deliveries in the city double to about 25,000 and riders look for relief from petrol costs.
body:
• Yulu has launched its electric delivery service in Nashik, starting with a fleet of 100 DeX electric two-wheelers operating from a hub in Rajiv Nagar.
  • The rollout is through Yulu's Business Partner vertical with Approach Auto Mobility, making Nashik its ninth franchise-led operation in two years and its 13th city overall.
  • Yulu says Nashik has more than 25 operational dark stores and 1,500 high-volume restaurants, and that city-wide deliveries have doubled in a year to about 25,000 a day.
  • The company claims riders on its EVs can retain 30-40% more earnings than on petrol motorcycles — a company figure published without a disclosed methodology.

Electric mobility platform Yulu has launched in Nashik, bringing its shared EV service for delivery partners to a city where doorstep orders have doubled in a year. The rollout starts in Rajiv Nagar and will expand across the city and surrounding areas based on demand, the company said.

The launch is under Yulu's Business Partner (YBP) vertical, in partnership with Approach Auto Mobility, a venture led by entrepreneur Jai Dhanani. Autocar Professional reported that operations begin with 100 DeX electric two-wheelers from a Yulu Centre in Rajiv Nagar.

Why Nashik, why now

Nashik is Yulu's second market in Maharashtra after Mumbai and its 13th city overall, joining directly operated markets in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi-NCR and Hyderabad, and franchise-led operations in Indore, Bhopal, Kochi, Tirunelveli, Madurai, Coimbatore, Kolkata and Chandigarh Tricity. The demand case is in the delivery numbers: more than 25 dark stores and 1,500 high-volume restaurants, with deliveries at about 25,000 a day, driven by instant-commerce and food-delivery platforms.

https://x.com/autocarpro/status/2115751005493379563

Most of those orders still move on petrol vehicles. That leaves riders carrying vehicle EMIs plus recurring fuel and maintenance costs — the gap Yulu's model is built around. Its plans bundle the vehicle with battery swapping through Yuma Energy and pricing that covers energy, maintenance and insurance, as Auto EV India reported.

The earnings claim, with a caveat

Yulu says delivery partners using its EVs can earn 30-40% more than those using petrol motorcycles. Both trade reports noted the same gap in the claim: the company has not disclosed the methodology or cost estimates behind the comparison. The direction is plausible — swapping is cheaper per kilometre than petrol, and maintenance is bundled — but riders weighing a switch should price their own fuel, EMI and maintenance bills against a Yulu plan before treating the percentage as a promise.

The expansion also tracks where quick commerce is going: out of the metros and into fast-growing tier-two cities, where dark-store networks are now dense enough to support a dedicated EV fleet from day one.

A franchise model doing the expanding

The Nashik launch also shows how Yulu is growing. Its four directly operated metros were built over seven years; the nine franchise-led operations, Nashik included, have all arrived in the last two. Under the Business Partner model, a local operator such as Approach Auto Mobility runs the city fleet while Yulu supplies the vehicles, the swapping network through Yuma Energy and the platform. That structure lets the company enter a tier-two city with 100 vehicles and a single hub, then scale the fleet against actual delivery demand rather than building metro-scale infrastructure first. If Nashik follows the pattern of Indore and Bhopal, the test will be whether dark-store density keeps rising fast enough to keep those 100 vehicles busy through the day.
